name: Every nonempty open real interval contains a rational (Archimedean property)

source.via: Rudin PMA Thm 1.20 / Eudoxus-Archimedes NAMED-NOT-READ. The Archimedean property READ verbatim in arXiv:1101.5652 Def 2.1 and arXiv:1204.4483 property (2); density READ as stated in arXiv:1101.5652 ('the rationals are dense in any Archimedean field', p.10 Lemma 3.4 proof; 'Q is dense in every Archimedean field', p.11 Thm 3.5 proof; 'Recall that the rationals are dense in an Archimedean field', Thm 3.8 proof) and in arXiv:2205.08354 p.10-11 ('both the Archimedean property and the density of Q in R are constructively valid (we have verified their proofs in the Agda proof assistant)'). Neither restating paper prints the density theorem as a numbered statement with its own proof; the proof is re-derived here (T1-T3).

published_statement: Archimedean property: arXiv:1101.5652 Def 2.1: 'A totally ordered field (ring) K is Archimedean if for every x in K, there exists n in N such that |x| < n.' arXiv:1204.4483 (2): 'For every x in R there exists n in N_R with n > x. Equivalently, for every x in R with x > 0 there exists n in N_R with 1/n < x.' Density: arXiv:1101.5652 p.10-11: 'the rationals are dense in any Archimedean field' / 'Q is dense in every Archimedean field'; Ex 2.7: 'The fields R, Q, C are all Archimedean fields'; Lemma 3.10 / 1204.4483 p.9: Dedekind completeness implies Archimedean. Hence for real a < b there is a rational p/q with a < p/q < b.
published_hypotheses: the ambient field is a totally ordered ARCHIMEDEAN field (1101.5652 Def 2.1; R qualifies: Ex 2.7, and Dedekind completeness => Archimedean, Lemma 3.10 / 1204.4483 p.9)
the interval is nonempty: a < b strictly (density is about open intervals (a,b) with a < b; T2d below shows the probe lemma fails at the boundary width exactly 1)
fails without the Archimedean hypothesis: in R(omega)/R(eps) ordered at infinity/0+, (0, eps) contains no positive rational (1204.4483 p.7; 1101.5652 Ex 3.9, sec.8); checked here as T4
constructively (Bishop reals, x < y meaning positive separation at some index) density and the Archimedean property still hold (2205.08354 p.10-11)
hypothesis_drift: NONE at the use site latticectc.py:38-47: the owner works in R (Archimedean), states A = |g1|^2 > 0 (latticectc.py:38) and H^2 > AC (latticectc.py:40), which together make the root interval (t-, t+) nonempty of width 2 sqrt(H^2-AC)/A > 0 (sympy T5b); a rational t = m/n in it with n != 0 gives Q(m,n) = n^2 (A t^2 + 2Ht + C) < 0 (T5a), and n = 0 is excluded since Q(m,0) = A m^2 > 0 (T5d). The lattice vector m g1 + n g2 is therefore nonzero and timelike exactly as claimed.

canonical.json restatement omits A > 0 (lists only H^2 > AC); the OWNER carries it (latticectc.py:38 in the theorem statement, latticectc.py:208 as an assert). A restatement omission, not an owner drift. Without A > 0 'between the roots' is not where Q < 0 (A < 0 makes g1 itself timelike, a separate case).

ADDED, unnamed, by the owner's constructive routine latticectc.py:203-216 (not by the external result): the termination sentence at :205-206 ('Terminates: once q > 2/width the interval q*(t-, t+) holds an integer') is true in exact reals -- the interval holds an integer once q*width > 1 (z3 T1), and the probe floor/ceil of q*mid lands in it once q*width > 1 (z3 T2) -- but the routine computes lo, hi in FLOAT (latticectc.py:209-210), which adds the hypothesis 'float-rounded midpoint within (q*width - 1)/2q of the exact one'. The RETURNED vector is always exact-verified (no false positive possible); only the stated termination bound fails. A discrepancy in the tree's own code, recorded not repaired; it does not touch the density theorem and does not touch D21's existence claim.

rederivation.outcome: z3 (5.1.0) + sympy (1.14.0), output in rederive/density-of-rationals.out. T1 unsat: y - x > 1 => x < floor(x)+1 < y. T2 unsat: width > 1 => floor(mid) or ceil(mid) lies in the open interval (the owner's probe); controls T2c (width 1/2) and T2d (width exactly 1) sat -- the lemma is not vacuous and the strict inequality is needed. T3 unsat: w > 0, q = floor(1/w)+1 => q w > 1 (the Archimedean step, nonlinear); T3b unsat: q(b-a) > 1, p = floor(qa)+1 => qa < p < qb, i.e. a < p/q < b. T4 (sympy): in R(eps) at 0+, p/q - eps -> p/q > 0, so no positive rational lies below eps -- the Archimedean hypothesis is necessary. T5a-d (sympy): Q(m,n) = n^2 q(m/n), root width^2 = 4(H^2-AC)/A^2, q(-H/A) = (AC-H^2)/A, Q(m,0) = A m^2. T6: owner's timelike_vector on 400 census spans, 400/400 exact, all within the exact bound. T7a: witness vertex 81/19 rational with q < 0. T8: float-rooted loop exceeds its stated termination bound (returns at q = 17479 against 3) on a valid input; result still exact.

later_literature.what: the Archimedean property (2) is strictly weaker than completeness and fails in every non-Archimedean ordered field (R(omega), formal Laurent series, surreals); density of Q is therefore a property of Archimedean fields, not of ordered fields in general. The tree works in R, so this narrowing does not reach its use.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite here: the result is a theorem about the ordered field R with no empirical input, so there is no datum the authors could have lacked. Evidence either way: (i) it is re-derived here from the Archimedean property in z3 (T1-T3, unsat) and has been machine-checked constructively in Agda (arXiv:2205.08354); (ii) its one essential hypothesis, Archimedean, is shown necessary (T4: R(eps)) and is satisfied by R (arXiv:1101.5652 Ex 2.7, Lemma 3.10). What the physical use would need is not a datum but the modelling hypothesis that spacetime coordinates/lattice generators are REAL numbers (an Archimedean continuum); that is H1 of latticectc.py (flat R^{1,d}) and is a named hypothesis of D21, not of this theorem. The only discrepancy found is in the tree's own constructive routine (float roots, T8), and it moves a termination bound, never a conclusion.
grade_evidence: Published statement (Archimedean property; Q dense in every Archimedean field; R Archimedean) READ via arXiv:1101.5652 and 1204.4483, confirmed constructively by arXiv:2205.08354. The tree uses it in R on a nonempty open interval (A > 0 and H^2 > AC at latticectc.py:38-40), exactly within the published hypotheses. z3 re-derivation unsat on T1, T2, T3, T3b with non-vacuity controls sat; sympy confirms the reduction Q(m,n) = n^2 q(m/n) and n != 0. No datum enters. The one discrepancy -- the float-rooted timelike_vector exceeds its stated 'q > 2/width' termination bound (q = 17479 vs 3) on a valid input -- is in the tree's own code, is not a property of the external result, and leaves every returned vector exact-verified; it is recorded, not repaired, and is not quoted as an error in the theorem.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree were shown to apply the density step outside an Archimedean field (e.g. over a non-standard or valuation-field coordinate model) or on a degenerate interval (H^2 = AC, the latticectc.py:52-56 boundary, where the interval is empty and density gives nothing -- the owner already treats that case separately). Nothing plausible makes the theorem WRONG or DATA-DEPENDENT. The T8 discrepancy would become a finding against D21's CONSTRUCTIVE claim only if a valid input made timelike_vector fail to return at all; that has not been shown.
